questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before a specific time in the future.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ my degree.

questions.def: Scheduled event in the future; use 'is scheduled to start'.
questions.question: The meeting ___ at 3 PM tomorrow.

questions.def: Fixed plan/arrangement; use present continuous for future.
questions.question: They ___ to Italy next summer.

questions.def: Simple future for a promise or immediate decision.
questions.question: I ___ you as soon as I arrive.

questions.def: 'is going to' expresses intention or prediction based on evidence.
questions.question: She ___ be a famous singer one day.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'by the time' when referring to the future.
questions.question: By the time you read this, I will be already gone.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous: duration of action up to future point.
questions.question: He ___ on the project for five months by July.

questions.def: Scheduled event; use present simple for future.
questions.question: The train ___ at 6:00 AM tomorrow.

questions.def: 'are due to' means scheduled or expected to happen.
questions.question: They ___ to finish the report by Friday.

questions.def: 'will' must be followed by the base form of the verb (see).
questions.question: I will seeing you at the party tonight.

questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before a specific time.
questions.question: The movie ___ by the time we get there.

questions.def: First conditional: present simple after 'if' for future.
questions.question: If it ___, we will stay home.

questions.def: 'will' is used for predictions without evidence.
questions.question: She thinks it ___ snow tomorrow.

questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before a specific time in future.
questions.question: By the end of the week, they ___ the project.

questions.def: 'will' expresses future ability or possibility.
questions.question: I ___ be able to help you tomorrow.

questions.def: 'will take place' is an idiom for a scheduled event.
questions.question: The concert ___ place next Saturday.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous: duration of action up to future point.
questions.question: By 2030, I ___ here for 20 years.

questions.def: Fixed plan/arrangement; use present continuous for future.
questions.question: We ___ having dinner at 8 PM tonight.

questions.def: 'intends to go' shows a firm plan or intention.
questions.question: She ___ to the meeting, even if she's late.

questions.def: 'is going to' for predictions based on present evidence.
questions.question: It ___ tomorrow, according to the forecast.

questions.def: 'should' expresses expectation or probability.
questions.question: He ___ be arriving any minute now.

questions.def: 'will hold' expresses an immediate decision or offer.
questions.question: I ___ the door open for you.

questions.def: Fixed plan/arrangement; use present continuous for future.
questions.question: We ___ them at the airport tomorrow.

questions.def: 'won't' (will not) is used for promises and firm decisions.
questions.question: I promise I ___ tell anyone.

questions.def: 'are you doing' - present continuous for future plans.
questions.question: What ___ you doing this weekend?

questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before a point in the future.
questions.question: By the time you arrive, I ___ the report.

questions.def: Scheduled events use present simple for future reference.
questions.question: The train ___ at 6:00 AM tomorrow.

questions.def: Arrangements use present continuous for future.
questions.question: They ___ to Rome next week.

questions.def: Future simple for spontaneous decisions or promises.
questions.question: I ___ you as soon as I arrive.

questions.def: "Will" is used for predictions about the future.
questions.question: I think it ___ rain later.
